correctness.rationale: Hyperelliptic split criterion over a degree-six P1 point is Tr_F64/F2(f(a)/h(a)^2)=0; all degree<=5 nonzero h (63 possibilities) give 9x11 binary trace matrices with rank histogram 3 of rank4, 60 of rank5, and the nine-ones vector never in the image. Fresh separately written GF64 binary rank checker reproduced this. Independently enumerated all 65535 nonzero cubic coefficient masks on each of the split/nonsplit/cone quadrics; computed (N6-N3-N2+N1)/6 from every F64 projective quadric point. Verified minima 1,0,2, exact nonsplit zero masks 28217,28280,29387,39919,59749 and all five F2 singularity witnesses by direct gradients. The Artin-Schreier degree-five gap and Weil bounds for n>=7 establish rho=6. Both genuinely finite classifications were exhaustively checked by independent implementations; no general inference from sampling.

value.rationale: The numerical threshold alone is already in Xarles census, but the theorem offers a constructive stronger splitting guarantee in the hyperelliptic double cover and sharp classification of all nonsmooth canonical section obstructions, useful for explicit finite-field curve/point constructions and boundary analysis.

final_claim: Every smooth projective geometrically connected genus-four curve over F_2 has degree-six closed points; structurally every hyperelliptic case has a split degree-six base point, and among all three canonical quadric types and 196605 nonzero reduced cubics exactly five nonsplit sections lack degree-six orbits and all five are singular. Bare rho(2,4)=6 is acknowledged implied by Xarles prior census.
limitations: Five masks are coordinate-dependent cubic representatives, not five geometric isomorphism classes.
Split-fiber guarantee is existence, not a count of all split fibers.
Bare rho(2,4)=6 is strictly covered by Xarles 2020 and must never be advertised as independently new.
Historical unindexed singular-section or splitting computations could duplicate structural components.
The finite canonical classification uses the specified monomial normal form, not geometric isomorphism classes.
